transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I just keep... blowing up at people. Over absolutely nothing. Like, the other day at the store—I work retail, and I manage this small team. Mostly younger kids, you know? Good kids, usually. Though this one girl, she always wears these massive hoop earrings, which is technically against the dress code, but I never say anything because corporate never visits our branch anyway. We're in this little strip mall next to a Panera, so it's mostly just regular locals coming in for... wait, what was I saying? 

Right, sorry. I was talking about blowing up. So, I completely lost my temper and just yelled at one of my employees. Screamed at him, really, just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. And afterward, I had to go to the back room and I was literally shaking. Because that is just not how I usually treat people. Normally I'd just fix the shelf myself, honestly, especially since those shelves are so old they wobble if you look at them wrong. We put in a maintenance request for them like three months ago and nobody ever came out... but anyway, yeah, the yelling. It really scared me.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

Oh, constantly. It’s like my nerves are completely fried. Like, if the store alarm beeps, or if someone bangs a pallet jack down behind me... actually, we have this one delivery guy, Gary, who brings our soda shipments on Tuesdays, and he is just the loudest person on earth. He always wears this neon yellow vest that practically hurts your eyes, and he complains about his wife's cooking every single week. Like, I get it, she burns the meatloaf, but I don't need to hear about it while I'm trying to count the register, you know? He always brings his dog in the truck, too. A little pug. 

But anyway, if he drops that pallet jack loudly, or if the security alarm goes off at the front doors—which happens all the time because the new cashiers forget to deactivate the tags on the expensive face creams. We sell this one cream with snail mucin in it, which sounds disgusting but people go absolutely crazy for it... wait, what was the question? 

Oh, right, being on edge. Yeah, if one of those loud noises happens, I jump so hard I almost drop whatever I’m holding. And my heart just keeps pounding and pounding in my chest for so long afterward, long after everyone else has just moved on and gone back to work.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Recurring thoughts... yeah. Honestly, it's the fire. It just keeps jumping into my head out of absolutely nowhere. Like, I’ll be at home and go to pick up a pan to make dinner. I have this heavy cast-iron skillet my mom gave me years ago. It’s one of those really nice ones you have to season with oil, you know? You can never use soap on it or it completely ruins the finish. My sister actually ruined one once by putting it in the dishwasher, and Mom was so mad she didn't speak to her for a week. She brought it up at Thanksgiving and made this whole dramatic scene about respecting nice things... wait, sorry, what was I saying? 

Oh, the thoughts in my head. Right. So I'll just be picking up that pan, or even just sitting in the back office at work opening an inventory spreadsheet—which takes forever to load on our ancient computers, by the way—and suddenly I’m just... I'm back there. I can literally smell the smoke. I see the kitchen just filling up with it, and it all happens before I can even stop it. It’s like I’m trapped right back in it all over again.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or activities because they remind you of the fire?

Yeah, I... I just can't. I've been completely avoiding the house. And the paperwork, too, like the mortgage folder. I can't even look at it. My husband usually handles the mail anyway, but he put the folder out on the counter. Our mail carrier, Dave, he always leaves the letters half hanging out of the box, which drives me absolutely crazy because if it rains, everything gets soaked. Last week it poured and completely ruined my favorite home and garden magazine. I love that magazine, they have these amazing articles on container gardening. 

Which... actually, that reminds me of the herbs on my patio. I had this beautiful little setup out there. Basil, mint, cilantro. I tried making homemade salsa with the cilantro once, but my husband says it tastes like soap to him. I read online that's actually a genetic thing, right? Like a mutation or something? My cousin Sarah has the exact same thing, she won't even eat at Mexican restaurants because she's so worried they'll sneak it into the food... wait, I'm sorry. What did you ask me? 

Oh, right. Avoiding things. Yes. The house, that mortgage folder, even just the thought of those herbs on the patio... if it's anything tied to that day, my chest just tightens up so bad. It's like I can't breathe. I just absolutely cannot make myself go near any of it.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the fire, as if it's happening all over again?

Reliving it? Um... well, I guess I kind of just mentioned that with the thoughts, right? Like when I smell the smoke. It feels really real. But actually, speaking of smelling smoke, someone was burning leaves in their yard the other day. Which I'm pretty sure is illegal in our town now. They passed some ordinance last year because the smoke was bothering people with asthma. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has terrible asthma. She’s always complaining about it at the neighborhood watch meetings. She brings these little lemon squares to the meetings that are so good, though. She uses real lemon zest, not that fake extract stuff. The extract always tastes like floor cleaner to me. I bought a bottle once to make a cake for my husband's birthday—he loves lemon cake—and it was just awful. We ended up throwing the whole thing out and going to Dairy Queen for ice cream cakes instead. Their ice cream cakes with the little crunchy chocolate bits in the middle are the best... wait. Did I answer your question? 

I don't really know if I have anything else to say about reliving it, other than what I already told you about the smoke and feeling trapped. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when you're remembering the fire?

Outside of my body... yeah. Actually, yes, that happens. Sometimes when I'm at work, just walking through the store, it feels exactly like that. Like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. The aisles, the customers... they're all there, but they don't seem quite real. It's like I'm just moving through them on automatic. We've been so busy lately, too. They put all the holiday displays up way too early this year. I mean, they had the artificial trees out before Halloween was even over. It's ridiculous. And those fake pine needles get absolutely everywhere. The janitor, Gary, he is always complaining about having to sweep them up. Gary is such a nice guy, though. He has this golden retriever named Buster who he brings pictures of to show everyone. Buster just had surgery on his paw because he stepped on a piece of glass at the park. Which is terrible, people really need to be more careful about picking up their trash. I always make sure to throw my coffee cups away, especially since they switched to those new compostable lids at the cafe next door. They're supposed to be better for the environment, but honestly, they just melt if your coffee is too hot... wait. What were we talking about? 

Oh, right. Feeling like I'm watching myself. Yes. It just feels like I'm not really there, just going through the motions on autopilot. It's a really strange feeling.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of blowing up at people and feeling anxious?

Two weeks. It's been about two weeks, ever since the kitchen fire. That was during our first weekend working on the house, which was supposed to be this big, exciting project. We had all these plans drawn up for the remodel. My husband found this amazing farmhouse sink on sale at the home improvement store, the one out by the highway. The traffic getting out there is always a nightmare, though. They've been doing construction on that overpass for what feels like three years. I don't understand how it takes that long to fix one bridge. Every morning the news says there are delays, and the newscaster, the one with the really nice hair—I think her name is Monica—she always looks so tired when she reports the traffic. I wonder what kind of hairspray she uses, because it never moves, even when they do those outdoor broadcasts in the wind. I tried using this extra-hold stuff once for my cousin's wedding, but it just made my hair feel like a helmet. It was an outdoor wedding, too, and it was so humid... 

Wait, sorry. The blowing up at people. Right. Yeah, it's been about two weeks, since the fire.
Do you ever find yourself back in the moment of the fire, reliving it as if it were happening again, without being triggered by a specific smell or sound?

Yeah, it does. It keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. I don't even need to smell smoke or anything. Like, I'll just be at work, opening a spreadsheet or picking up a pan at home, and suddenly I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up with it before I can even stop myself. Speaking of pans, I actually need to buy a whole new set because ours got ruined. I was looking at those non-stick ceramic ones online. They come in all these pretty colors now, like mint green and powder blue. My sister has the powder blue ones, and she says they're amazing, nothing sticks to them at all. She made this incredible cheese dip in one for the Super Bowl party she threw last year. Well, I guess it wasn't last year, it was the year before, because last year they went to Cabo for February. Which is such a weird time to go to Mexico, if you ask me. The water is still kind of chilly then. I went to Cancun once in January and I couldn't even swim in the ocean, I just had to sit by the pool the whole time. But the pool boy, Hector, he was so sweet, he kept bringing me these little frozen drinks with umbrellas in them... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Reliving the fire. Yeah, it just pops into my head completely unprovoked. It's awful.
Do you avoid talking about the fire or thinking about it on purpose?

Yeah, I try not to think about it at all. I mean, I've been completely avoiding the house. I can't even look at the mortgage folder on my desk, and I haven't gone near the herbs I planted on the patio because anything tied to that day just makes my chest tighten up and I can't make myself go near it. I used to love those herbs, too. I had basil, thyme, and this really wonderful rosemary bush that was finally starting to take off. Rosemary is so tricky to grow, you know? It always gets that powdery mildew if you look at it wrong. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has this massive rosemary bush that's practically a tree. She uses it to make this infused olive oil that she gives out in little glass bottles for Christmas. It's such a thoughtful gift, but honestly, the bottles she uses have these really cheap corks that always crumble when you try to open them. I ended up with cork bits in my salad dressing last time. I mean, I appreciate the gesture, but I'd rather just buy my own olive oil from that little Italian market downtown. The one near the old cinema? They have the best imported stuff, and the guy who runs it—Tony, I think his name is—he always gives you a free piece of provolone while you wait in line. Provolone is my husband's favorite, he puts it on all his sandwiches... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, avoiding things. Yeah, I just can't deal with anything related to the fire. It's too much.
Do you ever have vivid, visual memories of the fire that feel like you're reliving it?

I'm not really sure? I mean, I just mentioned how it jumps into my head, but I don't know if it's like a super vivid visual thing, like watching a movie. I don't really have a strong visual memory anyway. Like at work—I work in retail, at the department store over at the mall—customers will come in and say, "I saw this blue sweater on a mannequin here three weeks ago," and they expect me to just picture it perfectly. I can never picture it. 

The mall has been so dead lately, though. Ever since they closed the big anchor store at the north end, foot traffic is just terrible. Which is bad for my commission, obviously, but honestly, it's kind of nice not having to deal with the huge crowds of teenagers on the weekends. They always leave their empty Starbucks cups hidden inside the clothing racks. It is so gross. Last week I found a half-empty caramel Frappuccino that had been sitting behind the clearance coats for who knows how long. The whipped cream had turned into this weird, hard crust. I don't even understand how people drink those things anyway, it's basically just a giant milkshake for breakfast. My dentist told me the sugar in those frozen drinks will rot your teeth faster than regular soda. Dr. Evans, he's great, he has this really soothing voice and he always plays classical music in the waiting room... 

Wait, sorry, what did you just ask me? Vivid visual memories? Yeah, I don't think so. I'm not really sure what you mean by that, beyond what I already said.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or disconnected from the world around you when you're not thinking about the fire?

Yeah, actually, I do. It's the weirdest feeling. Sometimes when I'm just walking through the store at work, it feels like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. Like, the aisles and the customers are there, but they don't feel quite real, you know? It's like I'm just moving through them on automatic pilot. Speaking of the store, they just completely rearranged the shoe department, and it is a disaster. They moved all the women's boots to the back wall, which makes no sense because boots are our biggest seller right now. It's fall, everyone wants boots! I had this one customer yesterday who spent forty-five minutes trying on every pair of knee-high leather boots we had, and then she didn't even buy anything. She said her calves were too wide for them, which, honestly, they were, but I couldn't say that to her. I tried to suggest these really cute ankle booties instead, but she was dead set on the knee-highs. People are so stubborn about what they want to wear, even if it doesn't flatter them at all. Like my cousin, Sarah. She insists on wearing these low-rise jeans from the early 2000s, and they just do not work for her body type anymore. She wore them to our grandmother's 80th birthday dinner at the Olive Garden, and every time she reached across the table for a breadstick, well, you can imagine. The Olive Garden was so crowded that night, too. We had to wait an hour for a table, even with a reservation. The hostess was this young girl who looked completely overwhelmed, she kept dropping her little buzzer things on the floor...

Wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. What did you ask? Oh, the disconnected feeling. Yeah, it's exactly like that. Like I'm just floating outside my own body, going through the motions. It's really unsettling.
How long have you been avoiding the house and things that remind you of the fire?

It's been about two weeks. It started right after the kitchen fire, which was actually our very first weekend working on the house. We were so excited to finally start renovating, too. I had spent literally months looking at paint swatches for the kitchen cabinets. We were going to go with this really beautiful sage green. Green is super trendy right now for kitchens, you know? Though, honestly, I was a little worried it would end up looking like my Aunt Linda's house from the 1970s. She had those awful avocado green appliances. And the linoleum floor with the little orange flowers on it? It was hideous. Plus, she always smelled like mothballs and she used to make us eat these weird Jell-O molds at Thanksgiving. The ones with the shredded carrots and canned mandarin oranges suspended in orange gelatin? I don't know why anyone thought that was a good idea for a side dish. My husband actually likes Jell-O, but only the cherry kind, and he eats it with a mountain of whipped cream on top, which completely defeats the purpose of it being a low-calorie dessert. He buys those big tubs of Cool Whip whenever they go on sale at the grocery store... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, how long. Right. Yeah, it's been about two weeks, ever since that first weekend we were working on the house when the fire happened.
Do you ever find yourself suddenly back in the moment of the fire, feeling like it's happening all over again?

Yeah, it does. It keeps jumping into my head completely out of nowhere. Like, I’ll just pick up a pan to try and make dinner... which, honestly, has been a nightmare lately because we had to throw out half our cookware. I actually went to Target last week to look for a new non-stick skillet. They have that whole new line by that celebrity chef, I can't remember her name, the one with the blonde hair who's always making those thirty-minute meals on TV? Anyway, the pans are ridiculously expensive. Who pays eighty dollars for one frying pan? My mom always used cast iron for everything. She had this one pan that weighed like ten pounds, I swear. She used to make the best fried chicken in it on Sundays. We’d have it with mashed potatoes and this gravy that she’d make from scratch. I’ve tried to make her gravy recipe so many times, but it always comes out lumpy. My husband eats it anyway, bless his heart, but he drowns it in salt. His blood pressure is already borderline high, and his doctor keeps telling him to cut back on sodium, but he just sneaks the salt shaker to the table in his pocket anyway. It's like living with a giant toddler sometimes, I swear. And he leaves his socks everywhere, too... 

Wait, what were we talking about? I'm so sorry, my brain is just all over the place today. Oh, right, the fire. Yeah. So, I'll just pick up a pan, or even just be at work opening a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there. I can literally smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up with it before I can even stop myself.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're actually back in the kitchen when the fire was happening, like it's all happening again right now?

Yeah, I think... wait, didn't I just say that? I'm so sorry, my brain is just totally fried today. But yes, like I was just saying, it's exactly like that. It's not just a memory, it really feels like I'm standing right there in the moment. It just jumps into my head completely out of nowhere. I'll be staring at a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly I'm physically back in that room, smelling the smoke and watching the kitchen fill up all over again before I can even stop it. It feels incredibly real. 

Speaking of the kitchen, we actually still haven't gotten the insurance adjuster to come out and look at the damage. He keeps rescheduling on us. His name is Greg, and every time he calls, he has some new excuse. Yesterday he said his car broke down on the highway. Which, honestly, I get it, car trouble is the absolute worst. My Honda Civic started making this awful grinding noise last month. I took it to the mechanic down the street, Tony, and he tried to tell me I needed a whole new transmission. I was like, Tony, the car only has sixty thousand miles on it, there is no way. It turned out to just be a loose heat shield. Mechanics always try to upcharge you, especially if you're a woman going in there alone. My dad taught me how to change my own oil when I was sixteen just so I wouldn't get scammed. He was a mechanic himself, actually. He worked at the Ford dealership for thirty years before he retired to Florida. He loves it down there, he plays golf every single morning... 

Wait, I'm so sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yes, to answer your question, when those moments happen, it feels like it's happening right that exact second.
Do you feel guilty or responsible for the fire happening?

Guilty? No, I don't... I mean, I don't think it was my fault. It was an electrical thing with the old wiring in the wall, the firemen said. Which, honestly, is so frustrating because the home inspector totally missed it when we bought the place. We paid this guy, Bob, like five hundred dollars to walk through the house and tell us everything was fine. He had this little clipboard and kept tapping the walls with a pen, acting like he knew exactly what he was doing. He even brought his dog with him, this little scruffy terrier mix named Buster. Buster was cute, but he peed on the front porch right when they got there, which probably should have been a sign, you know? I love dogs, though. We’ve been thinking about rescuing a greyhound once the house is finished. They're basically just giant couch potatoes, which is perfect because I work on my feet all day at the store. The new manager at the store has us reorganizing the entire back stockroom this week, and my lower back is just absolutely killing me. I need to get one of those heating pads, the ones that you can plug in... 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, responsible for the fire. No, no, I don't feel like it was my fault. It was just the wiring.
Do you blame yourself for the fire happening?

I feel like you just asked me that, didn't you? But no, I really don't blame myself. Like I was just saying, it was the old wiring in the wall. The fire chief told us that before they even left the house that night. Chief... Miller, I think his name was? He had this really thick mustache, kind of like Tom Selleck. My mom used to love Tom Selleck. She watched Magnum P.I. every single week when I was a kid. She had this huge crush on him, and my dad used to tease her about it constantly. They had such a good sense of humor about that kind of stuff. They actually just had their fortieth anniversary last year. We took them to the Olive Garden to celebrate. You know, everyone makes fun of Olive Garden, but those breadsticks are honestly so good. I always eat way too many of them and then I'm completely stuffed before my actual food even comes out. I ordered the chicken alfredo and had to take almost the whole thing home in a little plastic box. My husband ended up eating it standing in front of the open fridge at like two in the morning. He's always doing that, waking up in the middle of the night to snack, and then he complains the next day that he has terrible heartburn. I keep telling him he needs to stop eating heavy dairy so late, especially with his blood pressure... 

Wait, I'm so sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. But no, to answer your question, I definitely don't blame myself. There was nothing I could have done to stop it.
Do you ever feel like you're disconnected from yourself or the world around you when you're not thinking about the fire?

Yeah, actually, that happens a lot. Especially at work. Sometimes when I'm walking through the store, it feels like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. Like the aisles and the customers are there, but they aren't quite real, and I'm just moving through them on automatic. Speaking of the customers, we had this one lady come in yesterday looking for a specific brand of organic cotton sheets, and she was so incredibly rude to my coworker, Sarah. Sarah is like the sweetest person ever, she just had a baby six months ago, a little girl named Chloe. Chloe is adorable, she has these big blue eyes and Sarah brings her in sometimes on her days off. I love babies, but they are just so expensive. Diapers alone cost a fortune now. My sister has three kids under five, and I swear half her paycheck goes to diapers and wipes. She buys them in bulk at Costco. Costco is dangerous, though, you go in for toilet paper and come out with a kayak and a three-pound tub of pretzels. I bought this giant jar of mixed nuts there last month and I'm still trying to finish it. My husband keeps taking handfuls of the cashews and leaving all the peanuts behind, which drives me crazy because then it's just a jar of peanuts...

Oh, gosh, I'm sorry. I did it again. But yeah, to answer your question, I do feel disconnected sometimes, like I'm just on autopilot and everything around me isn't completely real.
Do you ever feel like you're in a dream or like things aren't real when you're not thinking about the fire?

Wait, didn't you just ask me something like that? I feel like we just talked about this. But yeah, I guess it can feel like a dream sometimes. I don't really know what else to say besides what I just told you about how it feels at work. 

Speaking of dreams, though, I had the absolute weirdest one the other night. I was back in high school, and I couldn't remember my locker combination to save my life. Do you ever have those stress dreams? It's always the locker or forgetting you signed up for a math class. Anyway, my locker was right next to the cafeteria, and every Tuesday they made these awful square pizzas. The cheese was always burnt on the edges, but they had this homemade ranch dressing that was just incredible. My best friend Kelly used to dip her french fries in it every single day. Kelly actually just moved down to Florida last month, right near Orlando. She's been trying to get me to come visit and go to Disney World, but I haven't been there since I was twelve. We rode those spinning teacups and I got so incredibly sick. I can't do spinning rides at all anymore. Honestly, even just riding in the backseat of a Lyft makes me nauseous if I look at my phone for too long. I tried texting my manager back yesterday while I was in the car, and I had to roll the window down because I got so dizzy... 

Oh, gosh. I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry, my brain is just all over the place. What did you ask me? Right, feeling like things aren't real. Yeah, I don't know, it's pretty much just like I said a minute ago. I don't really have anything new to add to it.
